item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-f18fa0e25cce4a3a","start_unit":252,"end_unit":253,"fact_summary":"During 2023, the CNDH continued investigating the Ayotzinapa case and alleged official omissions, but reported that some authorities were reluctant to provide information: SEDENA and the FGR investigative unit generally collaborated, while SEMAR repeatedly refused cooperation. The CNDH stated that the victims still lacked full access to truth, justice, and integral reparations, and that only two of the 43 students had been fully identified.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns institutional conduct and unresolved accountability during 2023; attribution to the president is indirect because the document reports CNDH, military, and prosecutorial actions rather than a personal presidential order.","ruler_attribution":"The report concerns the federal administration and authorities operating under it, but does not establish that López Obrador personally directed the cooperation, refusal, or investigative failures.","limitations":["The report is an institutional account and does not independently adjudicate responsibility for the underlying disappearances or later investigative claims."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f18fa0e25cce4a3a","start_unit":253,"end_unit":253,"fact_summary":"After Hurricane Otis struck Acapulco on 25 October 2023 and rapidly intensified to category 5, the CNDH deployed a special team to inspect shelters, hospitals, migrant facilities, and military medical facilities; coordinated with SEGOB, the CNB, SEDENA, the Guardia Nacional, and state authorities; monitored rescue, reconstruction, debris removal, food distribution, and restoration of services; and returned 70 million pesos of its own budget to the SHCP for urgent relief tasks.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Direct evidence of emergency-response coordination and resource reallocation in 2023, although it primarily describes the CNDH's actions rather than the president's.","ruler_attribution":"Relevant to the federal administration's crisis environment and coordination with federal agencies, but the reported 70-million-peso reallocation was made by the autonomous CNDH, not identified as a presidential decision.","limitations":["The source does not provide outcome measures for mortality, displacement, service restoration, or distributional equity."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f18fa0e25cce4a3a","start_unit":257,"end_unit":260,"fact_summary":"The CNDH reported replacing its research staff through strict entry and periodic evaluations, forming a professionally qualified research team; it developed nine research lines, produced 20 academic works, conducted 160 academic activities with 284 national and international participants, reached more than 10,685 attendees, and convened a declaration involving more than 500 institutions around peace, equality, and human rights.","question_ids":["1B.7","1B.10","3B.4","3B.7","4B.3","4B.7","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Reports 2023 institutional staffing, research, and outreach activity; the broader four-year transformation context is also described but does not isolate presidential decisions in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The evidence concerns the CNDH under its own leadership and cannot by itself establish López Obrador's appointment choices, control, or personal support for these activities.","limitations":["Reported outputs are mostly institutional activity counts and do not demonstrate policy outcomes or independent quality assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f18fa0e25cce4a3a","start_unit":262,"end_unit":263,"fact_summary":"The CNDH created dialogue mechanisms on child protection and migration. A mechanism was established to prevent, certify, conciliate, and mediate conflicts involving human-rights violations against children, while a migration dialogue with more than 54 specialists agreed to form a working group and develop a progressive-policy indicator system.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.8","4B.3","4B.7","6B.3","6B.8","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Concrete 2023 institutional initiatives, with implementation beyond agreement formation not yet demonstrated.","ruler_attribution":"The initiatives were CNDH-led and involved government, legislative, judicial, academic, international, and civil-society actors; the source does not attribute them personally to López Obrador.","limitations":["The source reports commitments and planned indicators, not verified downstream effects or enforcement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f18fa0e25cce4a3a","start_unit":274,"end_unit":277,"fact_summary":"The CNDH reported strengthening international human-rights cooperation, receiving GANHRI A-status accreditation in May 2023, creating a monitoring system for compliance with international recommendations, assisting with 23 urgent actions and 12 precautionary measures concerning enforced disappearance and Inter-American cases, and conducting preventive coordination with authorities and civil-society organizations.","question_ids":["2B.6","2B.9","3B.4","3B.10","4B.3","4B.4","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly documents 2023 oversight and international-cooperation activity, but not necessarily compliance by the executive authorities addressed.","ruler_attribution":"The CNDH's autonomous actions and international standing provide context for federal accountability; they do not prove López Obrador's personal compliance or obstruction.","limitations":["The report does not state whether federal authorities fully implemented the recommendations, urgent actions, or precautionary measures."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f18fa0e25cce4a3a","start_unit":284,"end_unit":287,"fact_summary":"The CNDH strengthened planning and evaluation by monitoring program targets quarterly, evaluating programs, revising indicators, creating a Directorate for Monitoring and Follow-up of Institutional Commitments on 16 October 2023, building an open human-rights observatory, and using geospatial and public-source data to identify vulnerable groups and track rights conditions.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.10","4B.4","5B.7","6B.5","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Concrete 2023 administrative and monitoring changes within the CNDH.","ruler_attribution":"The actions are attributable to the CNDH's institutional leadership, not directly to the president; they are relevant only as a federal governance context.","limitations":["The source does not demonstrate that the monitoring changed national policy or improved rights outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f18fa0e25cce4a3a","start_unit":289,"end_unit":293,"fact_summary":"The CNDH reported restructuring, austerity, and resource reallocation: 93% of its approved 2023 budget was exercised, 69% of spending went to protection activities compared with 54% in 2019, official-event spending fell by up to 80%, public procurement was emphasized, and direct-award or three-bid procedures accounted for 4.61% of the authorized budget. It also reported suppressing 191 positions and reducing authorized staff from 1,885 to 1,700.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","6B.1","6B.4","6B.9","7B.3","7B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Direct 2023 institutional budget and restructuring evidence, while comparisons to 2019 span the broader administration.","ruler_attribution":"The reported budget decisions were made by the autonomous CNDH and approved through the congressional process; they do not establish López Obrador's personal direction.","limitations":["The report is largely self-reported and does not independently verify procurement quality, service quality, or effects of staff reductions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f18fa0e25cce4a3a","start_unit":297,"end_unit":299,"fact_summary":"The CNDH reported professionalization and merit-oriented personnel systems in 2023: 538 courses reached 1,165 staff; service-career evaluations covered 455 staff, 115 entrants, and 340 libre-designación personnel; 12 competitions were opened for deputy-visitor posts; and a pilot opposition-based competition for director positions was launched to increase transparency and exclude prior favoritism.","question_ids":["1B.7","4B.5","5B.2","6B.4","7B.5","8B.4","8B.5"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Direct evidence of 2023 institutional appointment and professionalization procedures.","ruler_attribution":"These were CNDH personnel practices, not appointments made by López Obrador's executive office.","limitations":["The source reports procedures and participation, not whether all appointments were ultimately independent or effective."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f18fa0e25cce4a3a","start_unit":303,"end_unit":309,"fact_summary":"The CNDH reported an autonomous Internal Control Body conducting 41 audits in 2023, addressing 160 pending observations and resolving 84, receiving 793 investigation files, processing 267 administrative-responsibility proceedings, finding responsibility in 53 concluded cases, and referring serious cases to the Federal Administrative Justice Tribunal.","question_ids":["4B.4","5B.5","5B.7","7B.2","7B.3","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Direct 2023 oversight, investigation, and sanctions evidence within the CNDH.","ruler_attribution":"The evidence concerns an autonomous oversight body inside the CNDH and does not establish comparable presidential conduct or executive accountability.","limitations":["Sixty-two observations remained pending; the report does not provide a complete assessment of sanction effectiveness or recovery of losses."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f18fa0e25cce4a3a","start_unit":315,"end_unit":316,"fact_summary":"The CNDH transparency unit handled 1,989 information and data-access requests in 2023. Of 58 review appeals, the transparency institute modified 23 responses, revoked seven, confirmed 16, and dismissed seven; the CNDH also updated transparency portals, trained 470 staff, and published public versions of 2,543 historical recommendations.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","5B.7","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Direct 2023 transparency activity and external review outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"The evidence concerns the CNDH, not a presidential disclosure or executive transparency decision.","limitations":["The external review modified or revoked more than half of the reported appeals, which qualifies the institution's compliance record; the source does not explain the substance of each case."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["This source is a CNDH institutional activity report. It provides indirect evidence about López Obrador's 2023 governing context and federal institutions, but rarely documents his personal statements, decisions, appointments, or responsibility.","The report is primarily self-reported and activity-oriented; many entries demonstrate procedures, outputs, or commitments rather than independently verified outcomes."]}
